chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: Keeping up with Tatum's strange keys and modulations
summary: Tatum worked in unusual keys like A, B and E; Stewart kept up by ear and found Tatum surprised and pleased.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now, when you -- you began working with Art Tatum in 1941. Is this the point at which you began to find yourself having to work in other keys or had you been working in the keys, began to expand the amount of keys you were playing with -- playing in rather when you had the Slim and Slam band?

Well, with Slim I worked in quite a few of those keys. Most of them I had before. Instead of working only in F and E flat, we started getting into keys like G, you know, and, of course, C sharp and C and even A flat, you know. I did a couple of things in -- when I started with Tatum, I was quite surprised that I was able to go along with Art Tatum in the key of A, some of those strange keys, you know.
Yeah, he liked B natural too.

And even E, some of those way out keys, which was quite an experience for me. And so I was so happy that I was asked to go along with it, you know, and at the same time be able to hear and get so that I could just about follow along with Tatum whatever he was doing, the changes he made.
Now, when you first started working with him, was he working with those kind of surprise modulations
Yes, he was. And that was a beautiful experience. I found that I was able to keep up with him.

He was surprised, very surprised. Come to find out, as time went along while I was working with him, I was his bass man. In other words, he loved everything that I did with him, and it was a beautiful experience.
